instructions: On Sunday, or up to 5 days ahead: Put the 6 eggs in a single layer in a medium pot and cover them with cold water by about 1 inch.
Set the pot over medium-high heat and bring it to a rolling boil. Put the lid on, take the pot off the heat, and set a timer for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, fill a large bowl with ice and cold water.
When the timer goes, transfer the eggs to the ice water with a slotted spoon. Leave them for 5 minutes.
Dry the eggs and keep them in their shells in a covered container in the fridge. They keep for up to 5 days.
When you want one, peel it and halve it. Put the halves cut side up on a plate.
Drizzle with a little of the olive oil and sprinkle on some of the everything bagel seasoning. Repeat with as many eggs as you're eating.
Serve cold, straight from the fridge.
advance_prep_notes: boil the eggs on Sunday, up to 5 days ahead
method_notes: Lindywell (the lead, 5.0 from 1 vote, visible rating, so it is a fallback) halves the eggs and tops them with everything bagel seasoning and a drizzle of olive oil. Its eggs boil for 6 to 7 minutes; this uses the common covered, off the heat method with a 10 minute sit (the one deviled egg recipes from Tasting Table and others use, not a source here) so the yolks are fully set and keep well for the week. The eggs are seasoned the day they're eaten.
